title: Signal consolidation and escalation orchestrator: telemetry-driven throttling and automated responder
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We continue to receive high-volume, low-actionability alerts across regions and services (cache hotshots, transient RPC spikes, model throttles). This increases on-call cognitive load and causes slow human escalation decisions. Goal: Build a signal consolidation+escalation orchestrator (a lightweight service + Alertmanager rules + runbook automation) that reduces noise by 60% for known transient classes, grades incidents by impact using telemetry, and triggers automated mitigations and only pages humans for high-confidence, high-impact events. The work covers SLO-aware grouping, region-aware circuit-breaker triggers, dynamic load-shedding policies, and deterministic automated responder actions for common incidents.
acceptance_criteria: >60% reduction in duplicate/low-value pages for target alerts in canary region over 7 days
Automated mitigations successfully resolve >= 70% of transient 'KV cache pressure' incidents without human escalation in staging
Escalation orchestrator computes a single severity score per incident using telemetry (error budget burn rate, latency p95 delta, region capacity) and only pages when severity > 0.75
Circuit breaker triggers (5% sustained error rate for 90s) cause deterministic routing to fallback region or degraded mode, documented and tested
Runbook automation logs all actions with auditable IDs and provides single-click rollback for each automated mitigation
tasks: Instrument signal fingerprinting pipeline (kinesis -> signal-enricher) and add deterministic dedupe keys
Implement Escalation Orchestrator service: ingest signals, compute severity, apply suppression rules, orchestrate mitigations
Add SLO-aware severity model (signal-ranker-v1) using error-budget burn + latency regressions + user-facing request fraction
Define circuit-breaker policy DSL and integrate with routing layer to support region failover and degraded QoS routes
Create load-shedding policy templates that prefer best-effort and internal traffic before customer-facing routes
Author automated responders (scaling, cache-flush, batching adjustments) with idempotency and rollback hooks
Wire up Alertmanager/Grafana -> Escalation Orchestrator webhook and test end-to-end in staging
Write operator-facing runbooks and Slack+PagerDuty incident playflows for edge cases
Canary rollout to eu-west-1 for selected alert families, monitor for false-negatives
decisions: Use telemetry-driven severity rather than static thresholds for first-stage suppression (decision made 2025-08-18)
Circuit-breaker trip criteria: region-level 5% error rate sustained for 90 seconds OR p99 latency > 2x normal for 3 consecutive windows
Automated mitigations limited to non-destructive ops: scale pools, toggle degraded routes, increase batching; no DB schema changes or customer-affecting config toggles without human approval
Fingerprinting window is 60s for dedupe + anomaly aggregation. Longer-term note: move to sliding-window fingerprinting based on trace IDs
Escalation Orchestrator will emit structured audit events to the console and append to incident timeline for observability
